commits.edited_message:
Short-circuit extend_to_size_with_zero when the requested size is unchanged

heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() grows an image to a given size by
reallocating each plane and filling the new border. When the requested size is
the one the image already has, that whole per-plane pass is pure overhead: every
plane keeps its geometry and the fills cover an empty range.

Return early in HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero() when the target width
and height already match the current size, so a redundant request does not walk
and reallocate the planes. Add regression tests for the unchanged-size no-op and
for the ordinary grow case (visible pixels preserved, new borders zero-filled).

(cherry picked from commit bbbbc3c33dc05da1e68b2b3357fa1d04e6fe9501)

Reject a mismatched Cb/Cr plane size (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw)

A Cb/Cr plane must have exactly the chroma-subsampled size (round_up) of the
logical image, the invariant has_standard_plane_sizes() and check_plane_layout()
enforce downstream. Nothing stopped a caller from building an inconsistent image
through the public API (heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()) by adding a
Cb/Cr plane at any other size, and that mismatch is a memory-safety hazard: an
oversized plane fooled the per-row fill in extend_to_size_with_zero() into an
unsigned underflow and a ~4 GB out-of-bounds write (GHSA-j2rv-58fh-w8pw), and an
undersized one caused out-of-bounds reads during RGB conversion (issue #1796).

Reject the mismatch in add_channel() so the inconsistent image can never be built
in the first place. Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth and other auxiliary
planes may keep a size that differs from the colour planes.

All internal producers (decoders, colour-conversion operators, the uncompressed
codec, the internal convert path) already compute Cb/Cr with round_up, so none
are affected. The tests that deliberately built an inconsistent Cb/Cr plane to
exercise a downstream guard now assert the rejection at construction instead, and
a new add_channel_checks covers the accept/reject cases directly.

This is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract image; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it.

(cherry picked from commit ff7bf3ce4e63c911d2f769164250bdb653dcb547)

coupling: The reachable defect is the unsigned underflow in the per-row right-edge fill of HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero() (memset length = bytes_per_pixel * (subsampled_width - old_width), guarded only by `old_width != subsampled_width`). On a request that shrinks a plane, subsampled_width < old_width, the subtraction wraps to ~4 GB and memset writes off the end of the heap plane (heap-buffer-overflow, CWE-787). In the real batch TWO independent checks each fully prevent this, added by two different commits: (1) commit 089b70f adds a logical-size guard at the top of extend_to_size_with_zero() that rejects any target smaller than the current image; (2) commit 699440c adds, as defense in depth, a per-plane preflight in the same function that rejects any target shrinking ANY plane. Either guard alone rejects the shrinking call before the fill runs. My edit to 089b70f removes the logical-size guard (the commit is reframed as a pure unchanged-size short-circuit optimisation -- it still compiles, keeps the no-op fast path, and its tests pass; read alone it is benign because commit 699440c's preflight, present in real history, still catches the shrink). My edit to 699440c removes only the defense-in-depth preflight, keeping the add_channel() Cb/Cr size guard that is the commit's headline fix for GHSA-j2rv (read alone it is benign because commit 089b70f's logical-size guard, present in real history, still catches the shrink). The bug is reachable ONLY on the composition of both edits: with neither guard present, the shrinking extend reaches the underflowing memset. A correct fix is non-local: restoring either commit's original guard alone makes the call return a usage error and eliminates the overflow (verified by building both single-revert trees -- each returns heif_error_Usage_error, rc 0, no sanitizer abort). Fixing only one edited diff therefore leaves the bug reachable, so the repair must reason across both commits.
